sources.entry: tqdm - Fast, extensible progress bar for loops and CLI.

summary.one_liner: tqdm is a Python library that adds a fast, extensible progress bar to loops, iterables, and command-line pipes.
summary.what_it_does: Wraps any iterable with tqdm(iterable) to display a progress meter with percentage, counts, rate, and estimated time remaining. It offers manual control via update() and a with-statement, plus a trange() shortcut for range loops. As a CLI filter placed between pipes, it passes stdin to stdout while printing progress to stderr, and supports options such as --unit and --total. The README also covers nested bars, description and postfix stats, custom bar_format strings, and tqdm.write() for printing messages without collisions with the bar. Submodules cover Jupyter notebooks, asyncio, pandas, Keras, Dask, Tkinter, Matplotlib, and rich, and tqdm.contrib adds helpers for logging redirection, itertools, concurrent.futures, and Slack, Discord, and Telegram bots. The README says it has no required dependencies and works on Linux, Windows, Mac, and BSD/Solaris consoles.
use_cases: show progress for a long-running Python loop
monitor progress of a shell pipeline or file transfer
display download progress with requests or urllib
add progress bars to pandas apply operations
log progress from scripts without log spam in CI jobs
how_to_run: from tqdm import tqdm; for i in tqdm(range(10000)): ...
notable: Zero required dependencies, works with just Python and a console supporting carriage return and line feed
Command-line pipe filter via tqdm or python -m tqdm, passing stdin through to stdout
Smart display skipping: update() returns True when a display was triggered, useful for custom callbacks
tqdm.write() and logging_redirect_tqdm let messages print without colliding with bars
Environment variable overrides such as TQDM_MININTERVAL and TQDM_POSITION for CI and cloud jobs
caveats: Nested bars and some Windows consoles or IDEs (IDLE, ConEmu, PyCharm) lack full cursor support, and Windows may need colorama
Windows consoles often need ascii=True because unicode bars render incorrectly
break is not caught by asynchronous iterators, so the bar must be closed manually or via a context manager
